items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and formatting is gofmt-consistent, but the doc comments are boilerplate ("Encode encodes the LaxLoop.") and nothing documents the ShapeIndex wire layout. The literal `maxEdgesPerCell > 1000000` has no comment explaining it.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: ShapeIndex.Decode is about 145 lines, over the 100-line cap. The code sits in shapeindex.go, not the requested shapeindex_encode.go. decodeShape calls p.Decode(d.r), which creates nested decoders instead of sharing the sticky one. The new readInt32 helper is never used.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every length is bounded before allocation, and shape, edge and cell IDs are validated. But a blanket `recover()` in Decode turns any panic into an error and can hide bugs. There are magic limits (1000000), and edge IDs go unchecked when `sh == nil`.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: New tags were appended without renumbering (`typeTagLaxLoop = 6`, `typeTagLoop = 7`, below typeTagMinUser). The Polygon, Polyline and Loop wire formats are untouched, the Shape interface is unchanged, and the Encode/Decode methods are purely additive.
